chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Madāʾinī, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about salat al-maghrib when its time has arrived: is it permissible for it to be delayed for an hour? He said, “There is no harm. If he is fasting, he breaks his fast and then prays; and if he has a need, he fulfills it and then prays.”

key_terms.تُؤَخَّرَ: to be delayed from the beginning of its time
key_terms.حَاجَةٌ: a need or matter requiring attention
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْمَغْرِبِ: the maghrib prayer whose timing is being asked about
key_terms.قَضَاهَا: he fulfilled or attended to it
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to delay salat al-maghrib after its time begins?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding salat al-maghrib after its time begins. It indicates that a brief delay is permissible, such as for a fasting person to break the fast or for someone to attend to an immediate need before praying.
